findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the width/height overload
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the 5-argument form is dead code and calls that pass width and height break. A call like `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` raises TypeError. A call with options raises ArgumentError because the arity is now 3..4. The removal of the `dimensions` helper is a further change to the public surface. Any existing caller using the old signature breaks. Keep one overload that accepts both forms, or update all callers and document the change.

findings.title: Animated GIFs over the limit are flattened to their first frame when animation is disabled
findings.body: The downsize call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When that setting is off, `optimize` uses `downsize_instructions`, which reads `#{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb line 129) and writes a single frame back over the uploaded file. An animated GIF larger than max_image_size_kb is therefore silently replaced with a static image. The setting governs thumbnails, not the user's original upload, so this destroys user content.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle, which rejects it
findings.body: `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `--resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` accepts only a WxH geometry, not a percentage. For GIFs with animation enabled, the conversion exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, and the GIF is never reduced. The controller loop then retries five times with no effect.

findings.title: Return value of downsize is ignored; failures are silent and the loop retries blindly
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when convert fails (`convert_with` returns false on a non-zero exit without logging). The loop ignores that result and decrements `attempt` regardless. A persistently failing conversion runs five times and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the original oversized file, with no log entry or error for the user. The comment 'automatically reduced to allowed size' is also inaccurate: a fixed 80% step over five attempts does not guarantee the file ends under max_image_size_kb.

findings.title: Up to five full ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes run inline in the request
findings.body: Each loop iteration runs a full `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` on the file. For a large photo that is several heavy external process runs. The synchronous API path (`render json: data.as_json` after `create_upload`) performs all of them inside the web request, which risks timeouts and ties up a worker. The reduction could instead be computed from the size ratio and done in one pass, or moved into the deferred job.

findings.title: Remote download cap hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: The URL download limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to a fixed 10.megabytes. Non-image attachments fetched by URL through the API can now be up to 10MB regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, and the admin-configured image limit no longer applies to downloads. Conversely, images over 10MB cannot be fetched by URL at all, which undercuts the stated goal of accepting large images. A failed download is still swallowed by `rescue nil`, so the user gets no clear error.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings and always uses 10MB
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It now hard-codes 10MB for every upload type, so max_attachment_size_kb is ignored client-side. Attachments above the configured limit pass validation, upload, and only fail on the server, and the user sees a message claiming a 10MB limit. The same hard-coded value at line 246 in `displayErrorForUpload` makes the 413 message show 10MB whatever the server actually accepts.

findings.title: SVG files that exceed the limit are run through the raster downsize path
findings.body: The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?, which covers svg (the client's isAnImage does too). `create_for` in optimized_image.rb special-cases .svg because it cannot be resized, but this loop has no such exclusion. An oversized SVG would be rewritten by ImageMagick, which rasterizes or corrupts the vector data, rather than being left alone or rejected.

findings.title: No specs for the new downsizing path or the changed OptimizedImage signatures
findings.body: The PR adds a downsize loop to the upload path, changes the OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, removes the dimensions helper, and changes limits in the client and the download path. No spec covers any of it. A single spec calling OptimizedImage.downsize with width and height would have exposed the duplicate method definition, and a spec on an animated GIF would have exposed the flattening and gifsicle issues.
